title: Jealousy and Envy
lead: Jealousy and envy, resentment of another's good and the rivalry it breeds, run through the Bible from Cain to the cross. The Bible also speaks of God's own jealousy, his claim on his people's undivided love, which is a different thing; this page is about the human vice. The New Testament lists it among the works of the flesh, and 1 Clement makes it the root of the revolt at Corinth.

sections.b: Hebrew qin'ah (קִנְאָה; not qinah, the dirge of the topic Lament) can be a person's burning zeal, a husband's jealousy (the law of the suspected wife, see the topic Sotah), rivalry, or God's jealousy for his people. Greek has two words. Zēlos is zeal, good or bad: Paul praises the Corinthians' zeal (2 Corinthians 7:11) and warns that "there is jealousy and strife among you" (1 Corinthians 3:3). Phthonos, "envy", is always bad: grudging another person's good. In the Greek letters the site keeps "jealousy" for zēlos and "envy" for phthonos (Galatians 5:20-21); its Old Testament also says "envied" for the Hebrew verb (Genesis 26:14; Genesis 37:11). God's jealousy in the Ten Commandments is his refusal to share his people with idols; it is not envy, which wants what belongs to another.
sections.refs: Exodus 20:5; Exodus 34:14; Numbers 5:14; 2 Corinthians 7:11; 1 Corinthians 3:3; Galatians 5:20-21; Genesis 26:14; Genesis 37:11

sections.b: The Bible's stories show what it does. Cain kills Abel (Genesis 4:3-8). The Philistines envied Isaac (Genesis 26:14). Joseph's brothers sold him: "Out of jealousy the patriarchs sold Joseph away into Egypt" (Acts 7:9). Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses, and Dathan and Abiram rebelled: "They grew jealous of Moses in the camp" (Psalm 106:16). Saul hunted David after the women's song (1 Samuel 18:6-9). In the Gospels Pilate "knew it was jealousy that made the chief priests hand him over" (Mark 15:10), and in Acts jealousy drives opposition to the apostles (Acts 5:17; Acts 13:45).
sections.refs: Genesis 4:3-8; Genesis 26:14; Genesis 37:11; Acts 7:9; Psalm 106:16-18; 1 Samuel 18:6-9; Mark 15:10; Acts 5:17; Acts 13:45

sections.b: Proverbs: "A calm heart is life for the body, / but jealousy is rot in the bones" (Proverbs 14:30), and "who can hold out against jealousy?" (Proverbs 27:4). Ecclesiastes sees all toil as "rivalry between a person and his neighbor" (Ecclesiastes 4:4). The Wisdom of Solomon says "death came into the world through the devil's envy" (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). The letters list envy among the vices of the old life (Romans 1:29; Galatians 5:21; Titus 3:3; 1 Peter 2:1), and James traces fights in the church to it: "Wherever jealousy and rivalry live, you find chaos and every vile practice" (James 3:16). Love "is not jealous" (1 Corinthians 13:4).
